status_summary: No charter that removes activity restrictions in exchange for higher equity or risk retention was found. The new licensing paths created since 2025 run the other way on activities: the GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27, signed 2025-07-18) set up a federal framework for payment stablecoin issuers with capital, liquidity and reserve requirements, and the OCC's implementing proposal of 2026-03-02 limits approved issuers to stablecoin issuance, redemption, reserve management, custody and directly supporting activities. These are narrow, single-purpose licenses, not the general charter the text describes.

timeline.event: The GENIUS Act (S. 1582) becomes Public Law 119-27, creating a federal framework for payment stablecoin issuers with capital, liquidity and reserve requirements (per the bill status summary). Listed as a parallel, not as progress.

The OCC proposes rules implementing the GENIUS Act for issuers under its jurisdiction, confining approved issuers to stablecoin-related activities and setting minimum capital requirements. Listed as a parallel, not as progress.

title: Create new financial charters with fewer activity limits for higher equity standards
uncertainties: No charter that removes activity restrictions in return for higher equity or risk retention was found. The GENIUS Act and the OCC's 2026 proposal create a narrow stablecoin license, and the March 2026 OCC chartering rule widens activity for trust-limited national banks without a capital trade; both are treated as adjacent. The OCC newsroom could not be read, and reported conditional trust charter approvals of 2025-12-12 were not confirmed from the OCC. The Unified Agenda rule lists on reginfo.gov for Treasury (including the OCC), the FDIC and the NCUA (headed 'Agency Rule List - 2026') list licensing and de novo chartering procedure changes and no new charter type. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
